answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent cannot transact until an established peer stakes its own bond on it, like a pilot guiding a vessel from the river out into the open ocean. If the newcomer is later caught colluding, the voucher is slashed alongside the fake. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must therefore recruit a thousand sponsors willing to risk real capital on each voyage, and every exposed fraud makes the next sponsor dearer, so cost scales with the fleet, not with cheap key generation.
